questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic opportunities in particular with regards to how well the courses available at the destination fit into my plans for my study. Also I wanted an exchange in Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the information I needed to get started at the University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any assistance but it felt like it was available in case I would have needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it very easily by getting in contact with student that went the year before and using their contact.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say that it works well, it is a city with an okay biking infrastructure and a very nice metro.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You needed to provide a list of different documents and information but they were fairly clear about what was needed early on so you had plenty of time to get it sorted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I felt I could always write them an email when in doubt and in general their response time was good.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just keep an eye on your email and if ever in doubt about what you need to do or when write to them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the level of the courses was okay, it was either to the same level as UCPH or lower but there is a difference in how far they are in the BA when taking some courses so keep an eye out for that as it naturally has an impact on the level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In style it wasn't too different from UCPH but the classes were much smaller and I would say that in general it was more focused on lecture and less so on exercise classes though there were still plenty of exercises to work with and prepare you for the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Macroeconomics III, Game Theory for Business, World Economic History, Public Sector Economics, Industrial Organization

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would in particular recommend Macro III as I really liked the way the class was structured and the teacher Luiz Brotherhood. Game Theory was also nicely structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any that I can think of

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was much cheaper than expected, you can buy a card for 90 days that covers a huge area for very cheap which you can also use to go on trips.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use this

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I very much enjoyed biking when I went but if this isn't for you I would recommend using the public transport card to go on trips to nearby places.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to smaller towns along the coast, get a bike if you can and go for trips. Go watch some football games, preferably from the lower leagues.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy the way the University works wasn't too different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they go out so much so the city in general is much more lively and it is easier and cheaper to go out for a cup of coffee or a vermut

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The academic level is lower but still worthwhile and you will learn so much more from the whole experience.
The coffee in the canteen is amazing.
There are a lot of Danes going on exchange here so be prepared.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your 90 day youth public transport card (app).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural and social experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say finding the time to do the things I wanted to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
